spec: CSS Custom Functions and Mixins Module Level 1

sections.1: 1 introduction this section is not normative note at this time this specification only defines custom functions which operate at the level of css values it is expected that it will define mixins later which are functions that operate at the style rule level custom properties give authors a lot of power to define useful sometimes complex values in one place and then re use them across their stylesheet they can vary across the document or based on media queries or other conditionals making them very flexible and responsive however their values are fixed at the point they re defined unable to be changed except by fully overriding their previous definition a shadow 2px 2px var shadow color declaration takes its shadow color value from the element it s declared on and later changes to shadow color on descendant elements don t alter the value of shadow for them they continue to use the shadow color defined where shadow was defined this is a common source of confusion for authors making heavy use of composite variables like this custom functions allow authors the same power as custom properties but parameterized they have the same flexibility and conditionality as a custom property definition but take values from other custom properties or explicitly as arguments at the point of use for example instead of a shadow custom property a shadow custom function could be defined instead like function shadow shadow color color inherit if shadow color argument isn t passed or doesn t successfully parse as a color try to use the shadow color property from the element instead var shadow color refers to the shadow color parameter rather than a custom property but can still use a fallback value as normal result 2px 2px var shadow color black foo shadow color blue box shadow shadow produces a blue shadow or just box shadow shadow blue tests function in media html live test source local inherit substitution html live test source local var substitution html live test source
sections.2: 2 defining custom functions a custom function can be thought of as an advanced custom property which instead of being substituted by a single fixed value computes its substitution value based on function parameters and the value of custom properties at the point it s invoked rather than the var syntax that custom properties use for substitution custom functions are invoked by dashed function syntax allowing additional values to be passed as arguments a simple custom function to negate a value can be defined as follows function negative value result calc 1 var value then that function can be referenced with negative in some declaration html gap 1em padding negative var gap or by passing the value explicitly like padding negative 1em dashed function s are arbitrary substitution functions like var their presence in a property s value causes it to be assumed valid at parse time and only evaluated and parsed at computed value time after arbitrary substitution has occurred

sections.4: 4 execution model of custom functions like the rest of css custom functions adhere to a declarative model the local variable descriptors and result descriptor can appear in any order and may be provided multiple times if this happens then declarations appearing later win over earlier ones function mypi result 3 result 3 14 the value of the result descriptor of mypi is 3 14 function circle area r result calc pi var r2 r2 var r var r local variable descriptors may appear before or after they are referenced
sections.5: 5 defining mixins a mixin is in many ways similar to a custom function but rather than extending upgrading custom properties mixins extend upgrade nested style rules making them reusable and customizable with arguments tests mixin basic html live test source mixin declarations html live test source mixin parsing html live test source mixin shadow dom html live test source for example the following code sets up a mixin applying all the properties you need for a gradient text effect including guarding it with supports queries mixin gradient text from color mediumvioletred to color teal angle to bottom right private gradient linear gradient var angle var from var to color var from var to supports background clip text or webkit background clip text background var gradient var from color transparent webkit background clip text background clip text h1 apply gradient text pink powderblue note that this example also uses a private property gradient which is accessible inside the mixin s rule to aid in readability but won t pollute the element s actual styles this is roughly equivalent to writing a nested style rule literally into the h1 styles h1 from pink to powderblue angle to bottom right color var from var to gradient linear gradient var angle var from var to supports background clip text or webkit background clip text background var gradient var from color transparent webkit background clip text background clip text except that none of those custom properties actually show up in the element s styles the entire mixin feature is experimental and under active development and is much less stable than function expect things to change frequently for now
sections.6: 6 private custom properties the private rule temporary variables are a common tool in programming languages letting one give a name to an intermediate result then use that name in another value to make it easier to read one can use custom properties for this purpose but they re automatically exposed to descendant elements on the page and might clash with existing custom properties used on the element requiring some degree of coordination between otherwise independent usages mixins make this problem even worse since its mixin parameters are exposed as custom properties for the applying element and its descendants to use to address these use cases the private rule can be nested inside of any style rule and defines private properties a special kind of custom property which is only usable inside the same style rule and any nested style rules private private declaration rule list the private rule is only valid nested as a child of a style rule or a nested group rule in any other context it is invalid a private rule can only contain custom properties and nested group rules in which case it passes this same restriction to their contents any other contents are invalid and will be ignored but do not invalidate the private rule itself when a style rule contains any private rules including those nested in nested group rules the set of custom properties they contain define the style rule s private property names a set of custom property names within the style rule and any nested rules any custom property with that name is actually a private property and any reference to a custom property of that name for example with a var is a reference to the private property a private property is a special variant of a custom property it is considered to be a different property from any non private custom property even if they share the same name two private properties with the same name are considered the same property if and only if they have the same nearest style rule ancestor that has their name in its private property names it is not exposed to the page via any cssom apis for example cssstyledeclaration getpropertyvalue can t get its value the cssstyledeclaration enumeration won t contain them etc it is only accessible to styles in the same style rule that defined them or its nested rules distinct private properties with the same name are for all intents and purposes separate properties they can exist together on a single element at the same time carry their own distinct values etc note because private properties are different from same named custom properties custom property registrations do not normally apply to them they apply to the non private custom property instead in some cases such as mixin parameters css can still give them a custom property registration applying a mixin with apply effectively substitutes the mixin in place so a mixin sees any private properties visible to the style rule it s substituted into if it doesn t override them with its own mixin parameters or private properties what about custom functions if they refer to a custom property not defined in the function should they see an outer private property i m inclined to say yes extracting some styles to a custom function should generally act identically to inlining them for example in the following styles every style rule is referring to the same custom property section size 2px border width var size section h1 size 4px section h1 small size 3px as a result the elements will have three different border widths if we changed that to use a private property in the first rule however section private size 2px border width var size section h1 size 4px section h1 small size 3px within the first section rule and its nested rules size is a private property and the var size refers to the private property in the later non nested rules size is a normal custom property independent of the private property from the first rule so setting it to other values won t affect the first usage instead it s roughly equivalent to section f7bd60b7 2px border width var f7bd60b7 section h1 size 4px border width var f7bd60b7 section h1 small size 3px border width var f7bd60b7 all three elements end up with identical border width values of 2px note while private properties ensure that elements and their descendants can t accidentally have their variables overwritten by accidental collisions they re still evaluated as normal for properties which can interact with other properties set in other style rules for example in the following variant of the previous example section font size 10px private size 2em border width var size section h1 font size 20px section h1 small font size 15px the styles are roughly equivalent to section font size 10px border width 2em section h1 font size 20px border width 2em section h1 small font size 15px border width 2em which will give three different border width values 2px 4px and 3px because private properties generally can t be registered custom properties if you did want the preceding example to resolve the em length against the section element you can t get that behavior by default this can be resolved with a custom function and might be addressed more directly in css in the future function as length x length result var x section font size 10px private size as length 2em border width var size section h1 font size 20px section h1 small font size 15px here because the custom function argument has type length it computes the 2em value against the element s font size returning 2px this then inherits as the px value to its descendants and is unaffected by changes in font size many of the example above work identically with mixins since mixin parameters define private properties notably whether a mixin parameter is typed or untyped can change its visible behavior in the same ways as the previous examples illustrated given the following two nearly identical mixins mixin untyped size border width var size mixin typed size length border width var size then in the following examples we get various behaviors section apply untyped 2px section h1 size 4px section h1 small size 3px in this example the size custom properties are distinct from the size private property defined by the mixin parameter so all three elements share a 2px border width section font size 10px apply untyped 2em section h1 font size 20px section h1 small font size 15px in this example the 2em is left unresolved in the mixin parameter so every element gets its own border width 2em value resolving to three different lengths based on each element s font size section font size 10px apply typed 2em section h1 font size 20px section h1 small font size 15px in this example because the mixin parameter is typed as length it resolves the 2em to 2px on the applying element and all three elements share a 2px border width
